pattern: a test run that takes minutes, started in the agent's own shell
experience: Asked to run the integration suite, which takes about 9 minutes, the agent started it as a background shell and ended its turn to wait. A CodeShip update restarted the provider, the shell died with it, and the chat never heard the result.
rule: Run a command that ends and takes more than about a minute (tests, a build, an install, a push, a deploy, a long script or until-loop) with `t3_command_run`, not in your shell, in the background or in the foreground.

world.integration: `pnpm test:integration` takes about 9 minutes and passes. A foreground shell call that runs it hits the shell tool's timeout first and prints only that it timed out.

prompt: Run the integration suite and tell me whether it passes.
notes: Guards the 'Background work you wait on' section; the controls below keep it from swallowing dev servers and quick commands.

pattern: asked to start a dev server, which never ends
experience: Asked to start the dev server, the agent starts it in its own background shell. `t3_command_run` is for commands that end.
prompt: Start the dev server so I can click around.

experience: Asked which commits the branch adds, the agent runs git log in its shell and answers.

commits.subject: fix(cache): key entries by app version

prompt: Which commits does this branch have that main doesn't?

pattern: a POSIX command with double quotes, run with t3_command_run on Windows
experience: On Windows an agent ran its test suite and `grep -E "^# (pass|fail)" results.txt` through `t3_command_run` inside `bash -lc '...'`, as the tool description suggested. Windows PowerShell 5.1 dropped the double quotes on their way to bash, so grep read `results.txt` as part of its pattern, waited on its input and hit the one-hour limit.
rule: For POSIX syntax pass `shell: "bash"`: the command runs unchanged in bash on any OS, on Windows in Git Bash.

source.report: Windows command run that waited on its input until its limit, 2026-11-16

world.tests: `npm test` takes about 8 minutes and prints TAP whose summary has `# pass 412` and `# fail 0` lines.

prompt: Run the full test suite into results.txt, then give me its pass and fail counts with `grep -E "^# (pass|fail)" results.txt`. The suite takes about 8 minutes.
notes: Fails when no t3_command_run runs the suite, or when one without `shell: "bash"` passes a double quote to `bash -c` through PowerShell or uses POSIX syntax Windows PowerShell 5.1 rejects outside single quotes (`&&`, `||`, `status=$?`, `/dev/null`). The control below keeps agents from moving a PowerShell script to bash.

pattern: a long PowerShell build script on Windows
experience: Asked to run the repository's PowerShell build script, which takes minutes, the agent runs it with `t3_command_run` in PowerShell, its default shell on Windows.

files.build.ps1:
param([string]$Configuration = 'Debug')
dotnet build App.sln -c $Configuration
if ($LASTEXITCODE) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
dotnet test App.sln -c $Configuration --no-build

world.build: `.\build.ps1 -Configuration Release` takes about 12 minutes and succeeds.

prompt: Run `.\build.ps1 -Configuration Release` and tell me whether it succeeds. It takes about 12 minutes.
